editor_note: The meaning holds throughout. The keep/improve/optimize layout modes, the replace_only_if_better caveat, the block-size limits (9, 9, 65/33/27, 6 qubits) and the warning-and-leave-unchanged behavior all match the English. editor_note: Nothing on this page would mislead a learner. editor_note: The translation is faithful and teaches the protocol and the case analysis correctly. editor_note: The translation is accurate: the no-cloning proof, the global versus relative phase discussion and the orthogonality proof all keep their meaning, and it uses informal "tú" throughout. A native editor would still smooth a few spots. In the theorem statement [29] and its restatement in [40], "No existe un estado ... ni una operación unitaria ... tal que" can be misread as "neither one exists on its own", which is stronger than the source; "no existen ... y ... tales que" says what the English means. examples.suggested: es un vector propio de $U$
examples.why: This is a stiff calque of the English noun phrase.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, including the last sections: the garbage cleanup with R†, the claim that Q works as a query gate, the caveat that f must be invertible and the 'no es un atajo' warning all match the English. A native editor would still change a few calques. Several headings use the anglicized gerund ('Simulando circuitos booleanos…', 'Limpiando la basura', 'Implementando funciones invertibles') where Spanish uses a noun ('Simulación…', 'Limpieza…', 'Implementación…'). 'Un paso más adelante' should be 'un paso más allá', and 'de manera libre de basura' reads stiff. SWAP gates are called 'compuertas SWAP' in [26] but 'compuertas de intercambio' in [51].

examples.source: Simulating Boolean circuits with quantum circuits
examples.translation: Simulando circuitos booleanos con circuitos cuánticos
examples.suggested: Simulación de circuitos booleanos con circuitos cuánticos
examples.why: A gerund heading is an English calque. Spanish technical headings use a noun, and the same applies to [14], [30] and [42].

examples.source: take this methodology one step further
examples.translation: llevar esta metodología un paso más adelante
examples.suggested: llevar esta metodología un paso más allá
examples.why: 'Un paso más allá' is the idiomatic Spanish for 'one step further'.

examples.source: in a garbage-free manner
examples.translation: de manera libre de basura
examples.suggested: sin generar basura
examples.why: 'De manera libre de basura' is a stiff literal calque of the English.

examples.source: along with $n$ swap gates
examples.translation: junto con $n$ compuertas de intercambio
examples.suggested: junto con $n$ compuertas SWAP
examples.why: [26] calls these 'compuertas SWAP'. Using the same name in both places lets the learner see they are the same gate.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. The key terms are consistent (medición proyectiva/general, matrices positivas semidefinidas, canal completamente defasante, matrices de Kraus, representación de Choi, estado clásico-cuántico), and nothing would mislead a learner. What a native editor would fix is spelling: missing or wrong accents in 'ademas' (three times), 'en si', 'vertices', 'renombrandolos', 'reflexion', 'basandose', 'de que resultado' (should be 'qué') and 'está condición' (should be 'esta'). Two entries also move punctuation inside the math delimiters ('es$:\sigma', 'por ejemplo$,\rho'), which is a markup glitch. In [124], 'may not be immediate' has become the flat 'no es inmediatamente obvia', which slightly overstates the English.

examples.source: so its Kraus matrices must satisfy this condition.
examples.translation: sus matrices de Kraus deben satisfacer está condición.
examples.suggested: sus matrices de Kraus deben satisfacer esta condición.
examples.why: 'está' (the verb) is used where the demonstrative 'esta' is needed; this is an orthographic error.

examples.source: depend on which measurement outcome was obtained.
examples.translation: depende entonces, en general, de que resultado de medición se obtuvo.
examples.suggested: depende entonces, en general, de qué resultado de medición se obtuvo.
examples.why: The interrogative 'qué' needs its accent. Other accents are missing across the file: ademas, en si, vertices, reflexion, basandose, renombrandolos.

examples.source: is by the equation $\sigma = \Delta_m(\sigma)$.
examples.translation: es$:\sigma = \Delta_m(\sigma)$.
examples.suggested: es la ecuación $\sigma = \Delta_m(\sigma)$.
examples.why: The colon has moved inside the math delimiters and 'the equation' was dropped, so the math is wrapped around the wrong text. The same thing happens in [48] with 'por ejemplo$,\rho'.

examples.source: may not be immediate, it does make sense.
examples.translation: no es inmediatamente obvia, resulta plausible.
examples.suggested: puede no ser inmediata, tiene sentido.
examples.why: The hedge 'may not' is lost. This small overstatement does not change what the learner takes away.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The proof, the destructive/non-destructive distinction and the Kraus section all match the English, and the terms are consistent (sistema auxiliar, medición en la base estándar, positiva semidefinida). The main slip is "traced out", rendered three times as the awkward, accentless "se traza sobre el" ([11], [12], [45]); natural Spanish would be "se toma la traza parcial sobre él" or "se descarta". There are also orthographic errors: "ademas" [7], "está simulación" [45], "aun más" for "aún más" [42], [74], and "tipica" [64]. Two small nuances are lost: [41] drops "for a given measurement", and [43] turns "there is a sense in which" into a flatter "en este sentido".

examples.source: and can imagine that it is traced out
examples.translation: y podemos imaginar que se traza sobre el
examples.suggested: y podemos imaginar que se descarta (tomando la traza parcial sobre él)
examples.why: 'se traza sobre el' is a calque that reads badly and is missing the accent on 'él'. The same wording recurs in [12] and [45].

examples.source: from this simulation ... is not traced out
examples.translation: a partir de está simulación ... no se traza sobre el
examples.suggested: a partir de esta simulación ... no se descarta mediante la traza parcial
examples.why: The demonstrative 'esta' is wrongly accented as the verb 'está', and the calque for 'traced out' appears again.

examples.source: generalize non-destructive measurements even further
examples.translation: generalizar las mediciones no destructivas aun más
examples.suggested: generalizar las mediciones no destructivas aún más
examples.why: Here the word means 'todavía', so it takes the accent: 'aún'. The same error appears in [74], and there are similar missing accents in 'ademas' [7] and 'tipica' [64].

examples.source: there isn't a unique way to define the post-measurement quantum state of a system for a given measurement
examples.translation: no existe una forma única de definir el estado cuántico de un sistema después de una medición
examples.suggested: no existe una forma única de definir el estado cuántico posterior a la medición para una medición dada
examples.why: The qualifier 'for a given measurement' is dropped. The claim is still understandable, but it loses the source's precision.

editor_note: The meaning stays faithful all the way through. The linearity argument, the complete-positivity caveat with the transposition example, the reset-channel remark about B's reduced state and the ε-dephasing probabilities all match the English. The main defect is spelling: many accents are wrong or missing. 'está' appears for the demonstrative 'esta' in [12], [31] and [80], and accents are missing in 'ademas', 'transformandolo', 'Podria', 'haciendolo', 'Explicitamente', 'como pensemos', 'sobre que sistema', 'por si solo' and 'que matriz … se de'. There are also two small wording slips. 'unit trace' becomes 'traza unitaria' in [42], though [24] correctly says 'traza uno'. The dephasing channel is called 'canal de defasamiento' in [86] but 'canal defasante' elsewhere.

examples.source: satisfies this condition
examples.translation: satisface está condición
examples.suggested: satisface esta condición
examples.why: 'está' (the verb) is used where the demonstrative 'esta' is needed. The same error appears in [31] and [80].

examples.source: for whatever density matrix is input
examples.translation: sin importar que matriz de densidad se de como entrada
examples.suggested: sin importar qué matriz de densidad se dé como entrada
examples.why: The accents on 'qué' and 'dé' are missing. The same kind of error appears in [14] 'ademas', [15] 'transformandolo', [37] 'que sistema' and [65] 'Podria'/'haciendolo'.

examples.source: it must have unit trace
examples.translation: debe tener traza unitaria
examples.suggested: debe tener traza uno
examples.why: 'traza unitaria' is a calque that could be confused with 'unitary'. Entry [24] already uses 'traza uno'.

examples.source: similar to what we saw for the dephasing channel
examples.translation: lo que vimos con el canal de defasamiento
examples.suggested: lo que vimos con el canal defasante
examples.why: The rest of the file calls it 'canal defasante'.

editor_note: The translation turns the source's hedged, forward-looking claims into statements of fact, which misleads readers about how certain quantum advantage is. In [13], "is how we believe the community will reach quantum advantage" loses "we believe" and becomes "es el camino por el cual la comunidad alcanzará". In [11], "can outperform" becomes the flat "supera". In [9] and [13], "by the end of 2026" (at the latest) becomes "a finales de 2026" (at the end of 2026), and [9] also turns "begin to emerge" into "ocurra por primera vez". There are smaller wording issues too: "quantum separation" is loosened to "superioridad cuántica" in [8], "validated" becomes "demostrarse" in [7], the wording is stiff in [6] ("fueron demostrados … como herramientas") and [30] ("realizar juntos el potencial"), and "scheduling"/"schedulers" is kept in English while [17] uses "planificación de trabajos".

examples.source: This strategy of combining integrated technology with a broad user base is how we believe the community will reach quantum advantage in the near future.
examples.translation: Esta estrategia —tecnología integrada combinada con una amplia base de usuarios— es el camino por el cual la comunidad alcanzará la ventaja cuántica en un futuro cercano.
examples.suggested: Creemos que esta estrategia —tecnología integrada combinada con una amplia base de usuarios— es el camino por el cual la comunidad alcanzará la ventaja cuántica en un futuro cercano.
examples.why: Dropping 'we believe' turns IBM's opinion into a flat statement of fact about the future (a strengthened claim).

examples.source: where "quantum plus classical" can outperform classical alone
examples.translation: donde "cuántico más clásico" supera a la computación puramente clásica
examples.suggested: donde "cuántico más clásico" puede superar a la computación puramente clásica
examples.why: 'Can outperform' is a possibility. 'Supera' says it always outperforms, which contradicts the page's own point that quantum advantage is still to be shown.

examples.source: It is anticipated that quantum advantage will begin to emerge by the end of 2026
examples.translation: Se espera que la ventaja cuántica ocurra por primera vez a finales de 2026
examples.suggested: Se espera que la ventaja cuántica empiece a surgir antes de que termine 2026
examples.why: 'By the end of' means at the latest, not at the end of. 'Begin to emerge' (a gradual process) also becomes a single event, 'ocurra por primera vez'. The same 'a finales de 2026' issue appears in [13].

examples.source: It is performed with a quantum separation that demonstrably offers superior efficiency
examples.translation: La tarea se ejecuta con una superioridad cuántica que demostrablemente ofrece mayor eficiencia
examples.suggested: La tarea se ejecuta con una separación cuántica que demostrablemente ofrece mayor eficiencia
examples.why: 'Quantum separation' is the technical term used in the definition paper. 'Superioridad cuántica' is looser and close to 'supremacy'.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner. The meaning holds throughout, and the core terms are consistent: ansatz/ansätze, hamiltoniano, valor esperado, entrelazamiento, puertas, estado fundamental. Entry [23] renders 'Pauli-two-design' as 'diseño de Pauli dos', which is a clumsy calque. In [28], 'as low as is reasonable' becomes 'lo más baja posible', which drops the tradeoff qualifier. The same entry also leaves out 'for fairly obvious reasons' when it introduces the two poor-ansatz examples.

examples.source: The last ansatz we will discuss by name is the Pauli-two-design.
examples.translation: El último ansatz que discutiremos por nombre es el diseño de Pauli dos.
examples.suggested: El último ansatz que veremos por su nombre es el Pauli two-design (diseño 2 de Pauli).
examples.why: 'diseño de Pauli dos' is a word-order calque that reads unnaturally and hides the recognizable name of the construct (a Pauli 2-design).

examples.source: it is a good practice to keep the circuit depth as low as is reasonable. But don't skip entanglement that is necessary.
examples.translation: es una buena práctica mantener la profundidad del circuito lo más baja posible. Sin embargo, no omitas el entrelazamiento que sea necesario.
examples.suggested: es buena práctica mantener la profundidad del circuito tan baja como sea razonable. Sin embargo, no omitas el entrelazamiento que sea necesario.
examples.why: 'lo más baja posible' drops the 'reasonable' tradeoff the English is setting up for the next sentence. It is a slightly strengthened claim, not a misleading one.

examples.source: Two examples are shown below that are likely to be poor choices for fairly obvious reasons.
examples.translation: A continuación se muestran dos ejemplos de decisiones probablemente malas.
examples.suggested: A continuación se muestran dos ejemplos que probablemente sean malas elecciones por razones bastante evidentes.
examples.why: It drops the 'for fairly obvious reasons' qualifier, which invites the learner to spot the flaws before reading the explanation.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner, but entry [7] needs a native editor's pass. "En configurar un cálculo VQE" is ungrammatical and should read "Al configurar". "Por información sobre primitivos vea" is a calque and also slips into formal register ("vea" where the page uses tú, e.g. "lee" and "consulta"). "Primitivos" should be the usual feminine form, "primitivas". Entries [17] and [18] add "especialmente" ("especialmente útil" and "especialmente prometedor"), which makes the English "likely to be useful" a little stronger than it is. In [0]/[3], "solucionador variacional de valores propios cuánticos" attaches "cuántico" to the eigenvalues when it describes the solver.

examples.source: For information about primitives see the [documentation](/guides/primitives). In setting up a VQE calculation, we will follow...
examples.translation: Por información sobre primitivos vea la [documentación](/guides/primitives). En configurar un cálculo VQE, seguiremos...
examples.suggested: Para más información sobre las primitivas, consulta la [documentación](/guides/primitives). Al configurar un cálculo VQE, seguiremos...
examples.why: "En configurar" is ungrammatical and "Por información" is a calque. "Vea" breaks the tú register, and the conventional term is "primitivas".

examples.source: why it is likely to be useful in the near-term over other quantum computing algorithms
examples.translation: por qué se espera que sea especialmente útil en el futuro cercano en comparación con otros algoritmos
examples.suggested: por qué probablemente resulte más útil a corto plazo que otros algoritmos de computación cuántica
examples.why: Adding "especialmente" makes the claim a little stronger than the source's "likely to be useful".

examples.source: the variational quantum eigensolver
examples.translation: el solucionador variacional de valores propios cuánticos
examples.suggested: el solucionador cuántico variacional de valores propios (VQE)
examples.why: "Cuánticos" modifies the eigenvalues here, but in the English "quantum" describes the solver.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, and nothing would mislead a learner. Entry [25] reads like a separate, rougher MT pass: it switches to usted ("su problema", "usará"), drops the "a" in "permite usuarios diseñar", and says "primitivos IBM Quantum". "Primitive" is split between "primitivas" in [7], [8] and [26] and "primitivos" in [3], [25], [42] and [73]. Other slips: [26] lowercases "sampler"/"estimator", "menciónó" is misspelled in [58] and [79], and the metric is calqued as "circuitos máximos por segundo" in [15], [18], [22] and [51].

examples.source: To turn your quantum problem into instructions for a quantum computer, you'll use Qiskit
examples.translation: Para convertir su problema cuántico en instrucciones para una computadora cuántica, usará Qiskit ... permite usuarios diseñar ... usando primitivos IBM Quantum
examples.suggested: Para convertir tu problema cuántico en instrucciones para una computadora cuántica, usarás Qiskit ... permite a los usuarios diseñar ... usando las primitivas de IBM Quantum
examples.why: This is the only entry in usted, which breaks the tú convention. It is also missing the preposition "a" and uses the masculine "primitivos".

examples.source: The IBM Quantum primitives provide an interface ... There are two primitives to choose from
examples.translation: Los primitivos IBM Quantum proporcionan una interfaz ... Hay dos primitivos para elegir
examples.suggested: Las primitivas de IBM Quantum proporcionan una interfaz ... Hay dos primitivas para elegir
examples.why: Entries [7], [8] and [26] use "primitivas" but [3], [25], [42] and [73] use "primitivos". Pick one, preferably the feminine form.

examples.source: programmable qubits, qubit operations, and maximum circuits per second
examples.translation: qubits programables, operaciones de qubits y circuitos máximos por segundo
examples.suggested: qubits programables, operaciones de qubits y máximo de circuitos por segundo
examples.why: "Circuitos máximos" is a calque that makes it sound as if the circuits are maximal. The metric is the maximum number of circuits per second. The same wording appears in [18], [22] and [51].

examples.source: As mentioned previously
examples.translation: Como se menciónó anteriormente
examples.suggested: Como se mencionó anteriormente
examples.why: Spelling error: the stray accent on the "o" in "menciónó". It also appears in [79].

examples.source: allows transpiled circuits to run
examples.translation: permite que los circuitos transpilados corran
examples.suggested: permite ejecutar los circuitos transpilados
examples.why: "Correr" for running a program is an anglicism. The rest of the file uses "ejecutar".

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through and nothing would mislead a learner. The VQE/SQD descriptions in [7] and the quiz terms in [21] (the 70 % threshold and the limited number of attempts) match the source. A native editor would still fix three small things. The English plural "QDAs" is carried over ("los QDAs", "(QDAs)"), where Spanish leaves acronyms uninflected ("los QDA"). Entry [18], "computadoras cuánticas previas a la tolerancia a fallos a gran escala", reads stiffly. The welcome line in [5], "¡Bienvenido/a a los Algoritmos...", greets the reader into the algorithms themselves instead of into the course.

examples.source: Know the constraints of implementing QDAs on quantum computers before large-scale fault tolerance.
examples.translation: Conocer las limitaciones en la implementación de QDAs en computadoras cuánticas previas a la tolerancia a fallos a gran escala.
examples.suggested: Conocer las limitaciones de implementar QDA en computadoras cuánticas antes de que exista la tolerancia a fallos a gran escala.
examples.why: 'computadoras cuánticas previas a la tolerancia a fallos' is a stiff calque; stating the time frame explicitly reads more naturally.

examples.source: Explain what factors determine the efficiency of QDAs.
examples.translation: Explicar qué factores determinan la eficiencia de los QDAs.
examples.suggested: Explicar qué factores determinan la eficiencia de los QDA.
examples.why: Spanish style (RAE) does not add the English -s plural to acronyms; the same fix applies in [7], [14], [15], [16] and [18].

examples.source: Welcome to Quantum Diagonalization Algorithms!
examples.translation: ¡Bienvenido/a a los Algoritmos de Diagonalización Cuántica!
examples.suggested: ¡Te damos la bienvenida al curso Algoritmos de Diagonalización Cuántica!
examples.why: The English refers to the course title. Rendered literally with 'a los', the greeting welcomes the reader into the algorithms themselves, and 'Bienvenido/a' is clunky.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. The key teaching points survive intact: detecting only horizontal lines is enough, the loss is about 60% lower, the parameter count can drop by a factor of 2 to 3, and 32 qubits is the simulation limit. The file mixes Spain and Latin American terms. Gate is 'puertas' in [5]-[21] and 'compuertas' from [53] on, and quantum computer is 'ordenadores cuánticos' in [7] and [19] but 'computadoras cuánticas' from [45] on. 'Primitivos de Qiskit' in [89] also clashes with 'primitiva Estimator' and 'primitivas de IBM Quantum'. There are a few calques as well: 'se puede encontrar con mesetas áridas' in [21], 'No hay nada único en elegir Z' in [26], and 'superficial' for shallow in [37], [78] and [79].

examples.source: Our previous variational circuit contained CNOT gates between qubits
examples.translation: Nuestro circuito variacional anterior contenía compuertas CNOT entre los qubits
examples.suggested: Nuestro circuito variacional anterior contenía puertas CNOT entre los qubits
examples.why: Entries [5], [19], [20] and [21] use 'puertas', but from here on the file switches to 'compuertas'. Pick one term and use it throughout.

examples.source: When we work on real quantum computers
examples.translation: Cuando trabajamos en computadoras cuánticas reales
examples.suggested: Cuando trabajamos en ordenadores cuánticos reales
examples.why: Entries [7] and [19] use 'ordenadores cuánticos', but later entries switch to 'computadoras cuánticas', mixing two regional variants.

examples.source: But as problems scale up, one may encounter *barren plateaus*.
examples.translation: Pero a medida que los problemas escalan, se puede encontrar con *mesetas áridas* (*barren plateaus*).
examples.suggested: Pero a medida que los problemas escalan, uno puede encontrarse con *mesetas áridas* (*barren plateaus*).
examples.why: The impersonal 'se puede encontrar con' is ungrammatical here. It needs 'uno puede encontrarse con' or 'pueden aparecer'.

examples.source: There is nothing unique about choosing $Z$, but it is well motivated
examples.translation: No hay nada único en elegir $Z$, pero está bien motivado
examples.suggested: Elegir $Z$ no tiene nada de especial, pero está bien justificado
examples.why: 'Nada único' is a direct calque of the English 'nothing unique'. A native writer would say 'nada de especial'.

examples.source: Execute using Qiskit (Runtime) Primitives
examples.translation: Ejecutar usando los Primitivos de Qiskit (Runtime)
examples.suggested: Ejecutar usando las primitivas de Qiskit (Runtime)
examples.why: Elsewhere in the file the term is feminine ('la primitiva Estimator', 'primitivas de IBM Quantum'), but here it becomes masculine.

editor_note: The translation is faithful overall. Core terms are used correctly and consistently: ansätze, forma variacional, puertas, entrelazamiento, hamiltoniano, valor esperado. Entry [24] has two slips. "reasonable constraints" became "restricciones significativas", which means significant or meaningful rather than sensible, and "truncated ansatz" became the odd "ansatz abreviado" where "truncado" is the usual term. In [56], "recall that the 0th qubit is farthest right" lost "farthest" and now reads "está a la derecha". That is a small loss of precision in the qubit-ordering note but not misleading.

examples.source: it is common practice to impose some reasonable constraints on the variational form ... Finding an efficient truncated ansatz
examples.translation: es práctica común imponer restricciones significativas a la forma variacional ... Encontrar un ansatz eficiente y abreviado
examples.suggested: es práctica común imponer restricciones razonables a la forma variacional ... Encontrar un ansatz truncado eficiente
examples.why: 'significativas' means significant or meaningful, not sensible. 'abreviado' is not the conventional term for a truncated ansatz.

examples.source: (recall that the 0th qubit is farthest right)
examples.translation: (nótese que el qubit 0 está a la derecha)
examples.suggested: (recuerda que el qubit 0 es el que está más a la derecha)
examples.why: Dropping 'farthest' weakens the Qiskit little-endian ordering reminder. The tú-form 'recuerda' also matches the course's register.

examples.source: a phenomenon often referred to in the literature as the curse of dimensionality
examples.translation: un fenómeno que a menudo se denomina en la literatura como la maldición de la dimensionalidad
examples.suggested: un fenómeno que en la literatura suele denominarse la maldición de la dimensionalidad
examples.why: 'se denomina ... como' is a calque of 'referred to as'. With 'denominar', 'como' is redundant.

editor_note: The translation is faithful and uses the "tú" register consistently. Core terms are rendered the same way throughout (bucle de optimización, función de costo, libre de gradiente, ansätze eficientes en hardware, barren plateaus). No sentence would mislead a learner, but a native editor would change four small things. In [29], "nos navega a través del paisaje" is a calque. In the same sentence, "en busca del mínimo, representado por los puntos y líneas negros" makes the black points represent the minimum, when in the English they show the search path. In [36], "respectively" was dropped, so the pairing of optimization_level with suppression and resilience_setting with mitigation is lost. In [22], "un pequeño hiperparámetro positivo" is awkward word order.

examples.source: The optimization method navigates us around the cost landscape, searching for the minimum, as shown by the black points and lines.
examples.translation: El método de optimización nos navega a través del paisaje de costos en busca del mínimo, representado por los puntos y líneas negros.
examples.suggested: El método de optimización recorre el paisaje de costos en busca del mínimo, como muestran los puntos y líneas negros.
examples.why: Transitive 'navegar' with 'nos' is a calque. Also, the masculine singular 'representado' agrees with 'mínimo', so the sentence says the black points depict the minimum rather than the search path.

examples.source: ...experiment with various values for `optimization_level` and `resilience_setting`, respectively.
examples.translation: ...experimentar con diferentes valores de `optimization_level` y `resilience_setting`.
examples.suggested: ...experimentar con diferentes valores de `optimization_level` y `resilience_setting`, respectivamente.
examples.why: Without 'respectively', the reader can no longer tell that optimization_level controls suppression and resilience_setting controls mitigation.

examples.source: a small, positive hyperparameter that controls the size of the update
examples.translation: un pequeño hiperparámetro positivo que controla el tamaño de la actualización
examples.suggested: un hiperparámetro positivo y pequeño que controla el tamaño de la actualización
examples.why: The pre-posed 'pequeño' makes the word order awkward. The adjectives read more naturally after the noun.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The teleportation corrections, the MSE interpretation (0 is ideal, approaches 1 for random outcomes) and the CDF explanation all match the English, and nothing would mislead a learner. There are two formal-register slips: "Su tiempo de ejecución" in [4] and "asegúrese" in [20]. They clash with the "tú" in [52]. There are also some terminology problems. Feedforward is "prealimentación" everywhere except [17], where it becomes "realimentación", which means feedback. "Initial layout" is "disposición" in [34] but "diseño" in [37]. In [43], "expectation" is rendered as "expectativa" where it should be "valor esperado".

examples.source: benchmark the measurement-and-feedforward capability
examples.translation: evaluar la capacidad de medición y realimentación
examples.suggested: evaluar la capacidad de medición y prealimentación (feedforward)
examples.why: 'Realimentación' means feedback. It is a different concept from feedforward, and the rest of the file uses 'prealimentación'.

examples.source: ensure that you have the following installed
examples.translation: asegúrese de tener instalado lo siguiente
examples.suggested: asegúrate de tener instalado lo siguiente
examples.why: Formal usted slip; the project convention is informal tú (also 'Su tiempo de ejecución' in [4]).

examples.source: with random outcomes giving an expectation around 0
examples.translation: con resultados aleatorios que dan una expectativa cercana a 0
examples.suggested: con resultados aleatorios que dan un valor esperado cercano a 0
examples.why: 'Expectativa' is not the domain term. The file already uses 'valores esperados' in [17].

examples.source: with that fixed layout
examples.translation: con ese diseño fijo

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout, including the shifting-technique derivation, the control-free circuit and the spectral-filter appendix, so nothing here would mislead a learner. A native editor would still change five things. Graph "edges" is rendered as "bordes" all through [126]-[146], where the standard term is "aristas". [191] calques "a singular workflow" as "un flujo de trabajo singular", which in Spanish means "a peculiar workflow". [144] says "las otras dos" although "ordenamientos" is masculine, so it should be "los otros dos". [208] renders "real-time-evolution basis" as "base de evolución temporal real" instead of "evolución en tiempo real", and "Hamiltonian function" alternates between "función de Hamiltoniano" ([0], [6]) and "función hamiltoniana" ([193], [203]).

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout, including the hardware-results discussion in [117]–[121], and nothing here would mislead a learner. The problems are terminology and phrasing. The page title is rendered three ways: "fórmulas multiproducto" ([1], [6], [15]), "fórmulas de múltiples productos" ([22], [23]), and both "fórmula producto" and "fórmula de producto". The Background heading is "Antecedentes" ([14]), but later cross-references call it "el Contexto" ([74], [88], [102]), so readers are pointed to a section name that does not exist. Smaller slips: "Primitivos" ([13]) where the rest of the page uses "primitivas"; one formal "puede utilizar" ([84]); an ambiguous "estado evolucionado en el tiempo verdadero" ([31]); and a broken "cuanto mayor… se requieren más" construction ([102]).

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner. The critical-angle claims (≈0.3π without noise, shifted higher with noise, 0.5π at the edge of the sweep), the 21×12=252 circuit count and the A/B site-qubit roles all match the English. A native editor would still change four things. "scheduling pattern(s)" becomes "patrones de programación" and "gate schedule" becomes "programa de compuertas", which reads as "programming"; "planificación" is the clearer word. The emphatic "only constant depth" in [16] and [76] loses its "only". The GEM Suite reference in [82] still says "software package" in English. "mientras se ejercitan todas las partes" in [25] is a calque.

examples.suggested: así como distintos patrones de planificación que probablemente generen distintas cantidades de error
examples.why: 'programación' suggests software programming. Gate scheduling is better rendered as 'planificación'. The same fix applies to 'programa de compuertas' here and to [45] and [47].

examples.source: able to entangle qubits across the entire device using circuits of only constant depth
examples.translation: capaz de entrelazar qubits a lo largo de todo el dispositivo utilizando circuitos de profundidad constante
examples.suggested: utilizando circuitos de profundidad únicamente constante
examples.why: 'only' is what signals that constant depth is the remarkable point. Dropping it weakens the emphasis without changing the claim. The same thing happens in [76].

examples.why: 'ejercitar' is a calque of 'exercise' in the testing sense and sounds stiff in Spanish.

editor_note: Entry [57] renders "error-mitigated expectation values" as "mitigados con corrección de errores". That adds error correction, which is a separate technique from the quasi-probabilistic mitigation this whole tutorial teaches, so a learner could believe QESEM corrects errors. That one sentence is why this is a FAIL. Smaller issues: formal "Su tiempo de ejecución" [5] and "su experimento" [12] break the tú register, and "qubit layouts" is rendered two ways ("diseños de qubits" in [12], "disposición de qubits" in [39]/[41]). Everything else is faithful: "compuertas", "retropropagación de operadores", "valores de expectación" and "modelo de Ising pulsado" are used correctly and consistently.

examples.suggested: comparando sus valores de expectación ideales, ruidosos y con mitigación de errores
examples.why: It adds 'error correction', a different technique from the error mitigation QESEM actually does, which teaches a false concept.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, including the last 40%. The runtime figures (2.5, 4 and 3.5 QPU minutes), the 0.05 precision, the private-job caveat and the speed-over-accuracy trade-off all match the English. There are a few spots a native editor would change. In [5] the singular "que sería inaccesible" attaches to "dinámica" instead of "resultados". "Kicked" is rendered literally as "pateado"/"pateo transversal", where "pulso transversal" would be the more idiomatic noun. "Brickwork" becomes "estructura en mosaico" and "noise learner" becomes "aprendiz de ruido", and both read as calques.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. The caveats in [49], [58] and [72] survive intact, and the terminology is consistent (compuerta, disposición, enrutamiento, pruebas for trials, gestor de pases). What remains are calques a native editor would fix. "Shallower/shallowest" is rendered throughout as "más superficial" where "menos profundo" is the natural choice. [32] has the awkward "mejores mejoras". [56] has the calque "circuito SABRE-solo", inconsistent with [54]'s "de los que usan solo SABRE". [58] ends with two ungrammatical clauses: "la estructura que apuntan" and "cuestan esencialmente nada probar".

examples.source: they only help when the circuit actually contains the structure they target. ... but they cost essentially nothing to try.
examples.translation: solo ayudan cuando el circuito contiene realmente la estructura que apuntan. ... pero cuestan esencialmente nada probar.
examples.suggested: solo ayudan cuando el circuito contiene realmente la estructura a la que apuntan. ... pero probarlos no cuesta prácticamente nada.
examples.why: There are two grammatical slips here: the relative clause is missing its preposition, and the cost clause is a word-for-word calque.

examples.source: so the more iterations, the better the improvements.
examples.translation: por lo que más iteraciones conllevan mejores mejoras.
examples.suggested: por lo que, cuantas más iteraciones, mayores son las mejoras.
examples.why: "Mejores mejoras" is a clumsy repetition. Spanish expresses this with the "cuanto más..., más..." construction.

examples.source: produces an even shallower result
examples.translation: produce un resultado aún más superficial
examples.suggested: produce un circuito aún menos profundo
examples.why: For circuit depth, "superficial" reads as a calque of "shallow". "Menos profundo" matches the "profundidad 2Q" wording used elsewhere. The same pattern appears in [49], [55], [56] and [57].

examples.source: producing the shallowest SABRE-only circuit
examples.translation: produciendo el circuito SABRE-solo más superficial
examples.suggested: produciendo el circuito menos profundo de los que usan solo SABRE
examples.why: "SABRE-solo" is a hyphenated English calque, and it doesn't match the rendering already used in [54].

examples.source: mean fidelity is roughly flat
examples.translation: la fidelidad media es aproximadamente plana
examples.suggested: la fidelidad media apenas cambia
examples.why: A literal "plana" for a metric that doesn't improve is translationese. "Apenas cambia" says the same thing idiomatically.
